name: Tasmania Road Safety Advisory Council (RSAC)
role: RSAC contributed to the development, advice and monitoring of Tasmania’s Towards Zero strategy. Government released the strategy; budget approval remains with ministers.
why: Separates advice, ministerial approval and state-level implementation; links sectoral partners to the 2017–2026 strategy and 2020–2024 action plan.
lesson: Make the council’s advisory mandate, ministerial budget authority and agency delivery responsibilities explicit.
caveat: Subnational state case. Full revised cell-level audit is not mounted in this session.

name: Conselho Nacional de Trânsito (CONTRAN)
role: National traffic council formally approved key Pnatrans policy instruments; secretariat and implementing agencies carry out detailed measures.
why: Restores council approval as distinct from plan drafting and ministry-level delivery.
lesson: Do not assign secretariat or implementation activity to every voting council member.
caveat: Direct ministry/partner split is unavailable from the latest audit file.

name: National Road Safety Council (MKKJR)
role: National council developed Road Safety Action 2030 and organized four action groups for enforcement, technical/infrastructure, research and outreach.
why: Adds previously omitted action-group responsibilities without equating the four groups with independent ministries.
lesson: Specialized action groups can distribute detailed missions under a single council.
caveat: Final formal-versus-partner domain split could not be retrieved.

name: State-Public Consultative Commission on Road Traffic Safety Problems
role: Commission endorsed and coordinated road safety strategy and operational planning; Council of Ministers is the formal approving authority.
why: July 2026 membership documentation and the 2026 operational plan identified additional ministries, assigned responsibilities and targets.
lesson: Distinguish policy endorsement, Cabinet approval, technical coordination and implementation accountability.
caveat: Measure 14 has numerical targets requiring confirmation; planned responsibilities are not outcomes.

name: National Road Safety Committee (NRSC)
role: NRSC and its secretariat co-developed the 2021–2030 plan with ministries and stakeholders; the Cabinet formally approved it.
why: Added the historical ministry roster, 2023 committee reappointment and 2025 cross-agency records, without treating older seats as confirmed current appointments.
lesson: Trace the historical roster separately from current representation and independent partner projects.
caveat: Detailed roster is historical (2005). A complete verified 2026 appointment list is N/A.

name: Canadian Council of Motor Transport Administrators (CCMTA)
role: The Council of Ministers approved Road Safety Strategy 2035+ in February 2026; CCMTA acts as intergovernmental custodian and coordinates technical committees.
why: Replaced the outdated RSS 2025-only interpretation; included five 2026 programme committees and separated optional interventions from jurisdictionally adopted actions.
lesson: Intergovernmental standards and monitoring are not equivalent to implementation authority over provinces or territories.
caveat: Group 2. An assigned national jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction implementation register was not confirmed.

name: Comisión Nacional de Seguridad de Tránsito (CONASET)
role: CONASET technically developed the 2017 road safety policy and the 2021–2030 strategy; ministries approve and implement actions within their mandates.
why: April 2026 third edition contains 152 proposed actions and evidence of civil-society participation, school programmes, enforcement and infrastructure plans.
lesson: Record policy authorship, concrete proposed actions, responsible agencies and observed delivery separately.
caveat: The 2026 strategy edition is a revision, not a new independent policy output.

name: Consejo de Seguridad Vial (COSEVI)
role: Statutory COSEVI council authored its Institutional Strategic Plan 2023–2030 and 2026 operating plan; other MOPT directorates carry out operational activities.
why: Confirmed five-seat board, budget and engineering/police functions, and incorporated the October 2026 Comptroller General audit.
lesson: An institutional strategy with funding and indicators is not automatically a whole-of-government national strategy.
caveat: STRICT POLICY ELIGIBILITY PROVISIONAL: the 2026 audit called for an integrated sector-wide plan, not yet verified as adopted.

name: National road safety plan implementation working group (MUP)
role: Expert drafting committee contributed to the 2021–2030 plan; the Government adopted it; the minister-appointed working group prioritizes, coordinates and evaluates implementation.
why: Directly recoded the 190-activity government plan and 2025 implementation documents against every defined ideal cell.
lesson: Government-approved action tables should name accountable owners, budgets, timing and evaluation requirements.
caveat: Verified source CSV available. Planned exact matches do not establish completed implementation.

name: Road Safety Council and seven interdepartmental committees
role: Statutory Road Safety Council and seven committees formulated the 2021–2030 plan; responsible departments implement its measures.
why: Detailed strategy and European Commission February 2026 assessment added governance, sector tasks and implementation-status evidence.
lesson: Detailed committee architecture still requires staff, financing, data infrastructure and independent outcome tracking.
caveat: EU assessment covers 26 programme areas, not the 158 strategy actions or our 72 scored interventions.

name: Government Council for Road Traffic Safety / BESIP
role: Ministry of Transport led preparation of the BESIP strategy, with council participation; council endorsed the 2025–2026 action plan, later government-approved.
why: The user requested a walkthrough, but a completed source-by-source recoding was not produced; retain first-pass figures pending validation.
lesson: Separate council endorsement from government approval and action-plan ownership; validate the approved activity matrix.
caveat: PRELIMINARY. Source summaries disagree on the F/P split (8/3 vs 6/5); leave that split N/A until reconciled.

name: Government Traffic Commission (Liikluskomisjon)
role: Government Commission endorsed the 2026–2035 programme prepared by the Transport Administration; the Government adopted it on 18 December 2025. The commission itself formally approved the 2026–2029 implementation plan on 18 February 2026.
why: Recovered the 2008 government founding order as revised in 2023, the current 2026–2035 programme, approved rolling 2026–2029 plan, named agency actions, financing gaps and 2025 monitoring report.
lesson: Separate Council endorsement, Cabinet approval, action owners, annual monitoring, budget availability and casualties; explicitly record when a plan action lacks an owner.
caveat: 2023 commission roster is a dated legal composition, not independent confirmation of every serving 2026 member. Exact labels are documented planned responsibilities, not completed measures. The approved XLSX implementation workbook was not directly inspected; explanatory memorandum verified.

name: Comité interministériel de la sécurité routière (CISR)
role: CISR, chaired by the Prime Minister, formally decided 38 national road-safety measures on 17 July 2023. The interministerial delegate/DSR prepares and tracks decisions; ministries, prefects, police and road authorities implement them. Separate CNSR advice is not counted as CISR decisions.
why: Corrects the original leadership-only 1/17 mapping using Decree 75-360 statutory ministerial roster, but distinguishes historical statutory offices from 2023 meeting attendees. Reassesses the 38 decisions and the 2025 road-homicide law against full 72-ideal wording.
lesson: Use a Prime Minister-led decision forum and permanent interministerial secretariat, but separate high-level approvals from accountable action owners, funded delivery and tracked outcomes.
caveat: 2023 decision package is a significant national policy instrument, not one unified ten-year strategy. Formal ministry names in the 1975 governing decree are historical, not a validated November 2026 roll call. Funding, programmes and casualty trends outside CISR are clearly labelled as context. 3 exact scores concern planned/adopted responsibilities, not proved public-safety effects.

name: Central Traffic Safety Measures Council (中央交通安全対策会議)
role: Prime Minister-chaired statutory council directly adopted the 12th Basic Traffic Safety Plan (27 March 2026, FY2026–2030). Cabinet Office prepares interministerial coordination; the distinct Traffic Measures Headquarters manages operational national campaigns; national ministries, the police, local councils, road operators and medical services deliver assigned measures.
why: Replaces an overbroad 13F membership classification and an undercoded 0 exact/8 partial checklist based on the 12th Plan and published statutory ministerial council roster. Road-traffic measures only, excluding rail, maritime and aviation. Financial-services council seat not conflated with ministry of finance. Separates the Council from Traffic Measures Headquarters and municipal/prefectural councils.
lesson: Separate high-level council adoption from Cabinet Office secretariat, Traffic Measures Headquarters, implementing ministry annual plans and prefectural councils. Pair national strategy with statutory local planning, specific education/enforcement/engineering/rescue measures and annual White Paper outcomes. Require costed interventions and named delivery ownership.
caveat: Source-based full 17-domain/85-cell audit of the official 12th Plan and statutory roster; A means an exact adopted or planned duty, not verified implementation. Some cells remain P when a national portfolio exists but the full checklist requirement (dedicated funding, data integration, formal training or cross-system rescue) is not confirmed. 2025 deaths predate the new plan. No claim that every delivery agency holds a central council seat.

name: Higher Council for Traffic Safety (المجلس الأعلى للسلامة المرورية)
role: Statutory Interior Minister-chaired Higher Council established under amended Traffic Law art. 17 bis (2023) and operating Regulation No. 2/2024. The Transport Ministry confirms contribution to national strategy preparation. The council directly adopted the executive plan for the 2024–2028 National Road Safety Strategy on 23 July 2025. Public Works, police, transport regulators, local administration, Amman Municipality and technical committees implement the actions.
why: Corrects 1/17 originally documented domains and 0 exact/3 partial 72-cell analysis using the official 2023 amended Traffic Law roster, 2024 council operating regulation, Ministry of Transport strategy-preparation record, July 2025 council adoption of 50 project and 28 programme cards, and February 2026 results reporting. Approved executive plan is attributable to council; detailed cards were not found online. Separate municipal and Central Traffic Technical Office functions are not misrepresented as Council seats.
lesson: Give the council a statutory strategy remit, real ministerial and operator representation, identified owners/funding/dates for an implementation plan and governorate/municipal coordination. Publish the action cards and independently evaluate outputs and casualty outcomes. Keep Ministry of Finance/Health/Education seats separate from planning, training and budget delivery interfaces.
caveat: Full official 2024–2028 strategy and the individual 50 project / 28 programme action cards could not be inspected; coding is deliberately narrow. Three exact matches concern the statutory national strategy lead and prioritization/treatment of high-risk roads; remaining specific interventions are partial or N/A. Statutory seats not actual attendance; reported progress not a causal impact evaluation. Do not equate the municipal committee with the Higher Council.

name: Road Traffic Safety Council (Ceļu satiksmes drošības padome)
confidence: Primary Latvian regulation and government-approved action tables inspected; revised planned-role coding; independent programme-effectiveness limitations.
role: Government-established consultative council chaired by Transport Minister, with Interior Minister as deputy. Coordinates policy planning and implementation, supports legislation, and allocates dedicated prevention funding subject to evidence requirements. 2021 national plan was drafted by Transport Ministry and adopted by Cabinet, not approved solely by council.
why: Revised from 11 to 15 documented domain links using 2026 Regulation 398 and its 28-seat council roster; re-coded 72 interventions using 2021 plan tables 18–20 and 2026 proposal / KPI / expert review / post-spending reporting provisions. This is a November 2026 view; July 2026 seats not retroactively treated as 2021 contributors.
lesson: Formal ministerial, public safety and municipal representation combined with NGOs, technical experts and insurers; continuous expert think tank, criteria-based annual allocation of insurer-funded prevention projects, mandatory KPIs and expenditure / results reports, and power to seek recovery of misapplied funds. Independent evaluation must still demonstrate effectiveness and sufficient national programme financing.
caveat: The 2026 regulation is CURRENT roster, not proof of who drafted 2021 plan. Transport Ministry leads strategy; Cabinet formally adopted it. Council is consultative except specific prevention allocation decisions. 33 policy measures are not 72 separate action outcomes. Ministry warns 2027 targets may be missed. 2026 regulation does not prove projects completed.

name: Group for Vision Zero Cooperation (GNS)
role: GNS is a multiagency cooperation forum linked to 2020–2030 target-setting; it is not the whole Swedish national road safety delivery system.
why: Separated GNS forum evidence from a wider road safety delivery-network assessment. The latter must not inflate GNS membership or its assigned missions.
lesson: Score the policy-contributing body and the national delivery network as distinct units of analysis.
caveat: SEPARATE CONTEXT ONLY: wider network = 15/17 domains, 12 exact, 19 partial, 41 unverified; excluded from the 17-profile total.

name: Road Traffic Safety Strategy Coordination Board
role: Board coordinates 2024–2027 Road Traffic Safety Action Plan through ministries and expert groups, including disaster-response representation.
why: Added AFAD representation from an official expert-group roster; functional score remains provisional without a complete intervention re-audit.
lesson: Count civil-defence and disaster preparedness only when their contribution is documented in the formal coordination framework.
caveat: 17/17 membership rechecked; 72-intervention score remains an explicitly provisional first-pass result.

name: Parliamentary Forum on Road Safety (PAFROS)
role: Parliamentary forum contributed to a legislative road safety action plan; it does not administer Uganda’s whole ministry-led national road safety strategy.
why: Kept the PAFROS legislative forum separate from the executive coordinating system and national strategy.
lesson: Do not assign national executive delivery responsibilities to a parliamentary policy-contributing forum.
caveat: PAFROS baseline retained; wider ministry-led system has not been recoded as this forum.

name: Strategic Road Safety Forum
role: Forum contributed to the Northern Ireland Road Safety Strategy to 2030 and subsequent action plan, with departments and local partners implementing assigned actions.
why: Official forum representation and the January 2026 action-plan annex supported a substantial revision from the previous sparse mapping.
lesson: Use the actual forum roster and action-plan annex to attribute responsibility, rather than inferred sector participation.
caveat: Devolved Northern Ireland jurisdiction, not the entire UK.

name: Governor’s Traffic Safety Committee (GTSC)
role: GTSC prepares, administers and monitors New York’s FY2024–2026 Triennial Highway Safety Plan.
why: Used the actual triennial planning document rather than generic descriptions of New York traffic safety programmes.
lesson: A committee’s programme cycle and grant allocation should connect to a documented annual and multiyear plan.
caveat: US state case. Planning match is not evidence of casualty impact.

name: Washington Traffic Safety Commission (WTSC)
role: WTSC formally adopted its commissioners’ Target Zero actions and co-developed a broader Washington road safety strategy with state, tribal and local partners.
why: Separated commission approval of the 2022–2023 action plan from broader 2024 partnership strategy authorship.
lesson: Distinguish the commission’s binding actions from policies co-developed with agencies and community partners.
caveat: US state case. Full F/P domain split unavailable in latest files.
